In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the diet on the development of NAFLD and NASH in a rat model.
the effects of dietary fat and carbohydrate on the development of NAFLD.
the effects of the dietary fatty acids on the liver and on the development of nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the consumption of monounsaturated fats (MUFAs) in place of saturated fats (SFAs) and carbohydrates (CHOs) is associated with a reduction in total body weight and fat mass.
the consumption of monounsaturated fatty acids is beneficial for cardiovascular health and may be associated with a reduced risk of developing diabetes.
monounsaturated fatty acids, in the form of olive oil or other sources, are beneficial to health.

the results of the study are consistent with the idea that the presence of a high level of cholesterol in the liver can cause a reduction in the amount of fat in the liver.

the data support the hypothesis that a diet plan rich in monounsaturated fats is beneficial to non-alcoholic fatty disease.

the effects of a high-fat diet are dependent on the source and type of fat.
the effects of a low-fat diet are not limited to the liver.
